description: REQ-010 says 'run.sh reads $CAP's content, appends "\n\u200b#c<clip_id>" ... and passes THIS appended string to post_reel.py as the caption to insert.' This is not implementable as literally written: post_reel.py's ONLY caption-input mechanism is the CLI flag `--caption-file <path>`, which it opens and reads directly (`caption = open(a.caption_file, encoding="utf-8").read().strip()`, post_reel.py:86; `ap.add_argument("--caption-file", required=True)`, post_reel.py:78) -- there is no `--caption-text`/stdin/inline-string interface. run.sh's existing invocation (`"$PY" "$POSTER" --video "$CLIP" --caption-file "$CAP" ...`, run.sh:88) passes a FILE PATH, not string content. For REQ-010's token-appended text to actually reach post_reel.py, run.sh MUST materialize it as a file on disk and pass THAT path as `--caption-file` -- but the spec never says how: (a) does run.sh write a NEW temp file (where, what name, cleaned up when/how, on every attempt including retries)? (b) does run.sh mutate `$CAP` in place before the POSTER call? If (b), this is actively dangerous: `$CAP` is the SAME file that (per REQ-007) stays in `$CLIP_QUEUE` and gets RE-ATTEMPTED on a later wake after a 'failed' outcome -- if the token were appended in-place each attempt without being reverted, a clip retried N times would accumulate N stacked token lines in its permanently-queued/posted caption sidecar, and (per run.sh:94-95) the (by-then-mutated) $CAP file itself gets moved to $CLIP_POSTED alongside the video on success, silently changing the on-disk caption artifact from what was originally produced. Neither option is specified, tested, or even mentioned as a design decision anywhere in REQ-010, REQ-008, or the verification-architecture.md pseudocode block (which only shows the post_reel.py-internal before/candidate/reconfirm logic, not any run.sh-side change to the POSTER invocation). This is the same class of gap iteration-9's FIND-021 and iteration-10's FIND-027 both caught (missing concrete plumbing for a cross-file data path) -- REQ-010, this iteration's core fix for FIND-025, has an identical unaddressed plumbing gap of its own, and it sits directly on the path of every single live post attempt, not just the self-heal path.
